decisions.title: Read your observed dexterous prayer scroll
decisions.why: The scroll can unlock Rigour, a permanent ranged prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts already using Bowfa or a twisted bow. Keeping the scroll in storage provides no permanent unlock.
decisions.alternative: Keep using your currently available lower-level prayers and save the scroll if you deliberately want a spare. Another gear grind is not required to read this owned scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Reading consumes this scroll. The unlock remains after consumption; it does not prove that your levels already allow using the prayer.
decisions.effort: Small one-off action once the observed scroll is retrieved and unnoted. No drop grind or time estimate.
decisions.access: An observed scroll and confirmed locked prayer; no skill requirement to read. Retrieve from bank first if needed.
decisions.completion: Rigour unlock varbit is true; scroll absence is never completion evidence.
decisions.applicability: A positive inventory/equipment/session-bank observation of the exact scroll and a known false unlock.
notes: Reading has no skill requirement; using the prayer needs its documented Prayer and Defence levels. Scroll possession and permanent unlocks are different facts.
decisions.preparation: A positive inventory/equipment/session-bank observation of the exact scroll and a known false unlock.
decisions.benefitReason: Confirmed locked permanent prayer with an observed scroll.

decisions.title: Train Prayer to 74 for your unlocked Rigour
decisions.why: You already unlocked Rigour, a permanent ranged prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts already using Bowfa or a twisted bow. Prayer levels are the remaining confirmed gap to using it with your observed Defence level.
decisions.alternative: Use your currently available lower-level prayers and practise team CoX while building supplies. You do not need another dexterous scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Training uses bones and other supplies that could support different account goals. This is an optional preparation upgrade, not a raid entry requirement.
decisions.effort: Supply-dependent training; gathering and training method are outside this catalogue. No exact hours or RNG forecast.
decisions.access: Ordinary Prayer training; the catalogue applies only with confirmed unlock and 70+ Defence.
decisions.completion: Real Prayer level is at least 74.
decisions.applicability: Confirmed permanent unlock, known Prayer below 74, and known Defence at least 70.
decisions.preparation: Confirmed permanent unlock, known Prayer below 74, and known Defence at least 70.
decisions.benefitReason: Confirmed Prayer gap for an unlocked prayer; a selected goal can put its own training first.

decisions.title: Plan ordinary team CoX with your observed weapons
decisions.why: You have recognised weapons across three styles and meet this catalogue's stated planning baseline. Agreeing a team setup with these options can be more useful than postponing practice for another weapon grind. This remains a repeatable prompt; raid history and player skill are unknown.
decisions.alternative: Use your observed rune crossbow if you decline CG; Bowfa with active crystal armour and a twisted bow are other recognised options. Dragon hunter crossbows, eclipse atlatl setups and dragon hunter wand spell setups appear in current CoX guidance but are outside this baseline. Review those with your team or a specialist planner; no mandatory Bowfa route is implied.
decisions.tradeoff: A learner team must agree your setup and supply roles. This catalogue does not establish raid access, armour completeness, weapon access unlocks, charges, ammunition, supplies or player skill. It does not certify solo or Challenge Mode readiness.
decisions.effort: Team coordination and practice; repeatable planning opportunity, not an inferred unfinished account unlock. Learning time varies.
decisions.access: Planning has no game requirement. CoX entry separately needs access to Great Kourend, which is unobserved. Equipping a lance additionally needs the Firemaking (not pyre), Fishing and Smithing sections of Barbarian Training; these unlocks are unobserved. Crystal equipment has quest requirements; this catalogue does not verify them.
decisions.completion: Repeatable planning prompt; no raid history is observed and no first-kill claim is made.
decisions.applicability: 80+ Attack/Strength/Ranged/Magic/Hitpoints and 70+ Defence/Prayer (authored preparation baseline, not game access); recognised positive weapons and their wield levels. Bowfa selection additionally needs observed active crystal pieces and 70 Agility.
notes: The checked skill and three-style baseline is authored preparation, not game access. Team roles, full raid switches, supplies and actual access remain unverified.
decisions.preparation: 80+ Attack/Strength/Ranged/Magic/Hitpoints and 70+ Defence/Prayer (authored preparation baseline, not game access); recognised positive weapons and their wield levels. Bowfa selection additionally needs observed active crystal pieces and 70 Agility.
decisions.benefitReason: Recognised three-style kit supports ordinary team preparation.

decisions.title: Assemble a swamp trident from your observed magic fang
decisions.why: You have a magic fang and a seas trident. A swamp trident gives your CoX magic kit a stronger built-in spell without starting another weapon drop grind. This can still help a Bowfa account whose magic weapon remains a seas trident.
decisions.alternative: Keep using the seas trident if scale upkeep is unwelcome. An owned swamp trident, Sanguinesti staff, Eye of Ayak, Shadow or dragon hunter wand suppresses this assembly prompt; compare that option first. The wand needs a suitable spellbook, spells and runes, so possession alone does not establish a usable spell setup.
decisions.tradeoff: Uncharge the seas trident before assembly, retrieve and unnote components, then arrange runes and Zulrah scales. Using scales adds upkeep. A fang used here is unavailable for a toxic staff of the dead unless the trident is dismantled. No charges or supply quantities are inferred.
decisions.effort: Small assembly with owned parts; recurring scale and rune supplies vary with use. No drop-time estimate.
decisions.access: Assembly requires 59 Crafting, a chisel, magic fang and uncharged seas trident; enhanced seas tridents also work. Charging and wielding the result requires 78 Magic. Known real levels meet the thresholds; temporary boosts are not modelled.
decisions.completion: A recognised swamp trident (including uncharged/enhanced) or competing owned magic option ends this bounded assembly suggestion; this is not a claim that every alternative is best everywhere.
decisions.applicability: Positive fang, chisel and seas-trident observations; known Crafting 59+ and Magic 78+; completion must be confirmed false in supported storage. Unobserved containers keep completion unknown.
notes: No recognised competing magic option observed in supported storage; other storage remains unknown. Check before assembly.
decisions.preparation: Positive fang, chisel and seas-trident observations; known Crafting 59+ and Magic 78+; completion must be confirmed false in supported storage. Unobserved containers keep completion unknown.
decisions.benefitReason: Owned parts, no supported observed/manual competing magic option.

decisions.title: Compare your owned lance for the Olm melee role
decisions.why: You have a dragon hunter lance alongside a whip, tentacle or fang. Its dragonbane effect applies to Olm, so it is worth reviewing for that melee role even when your ranged kit is already established. This comparison does not call it the best weapon for every raid room.
decisions.alternative: Keep the whip or tentacle for a familiar setup, or retain the fang where its stab role suits your room plan. An observed scythe or Soulreaper axe suppresses this narrow comparison; use a specialist comparison for those weapons rather than assuming the lance wins.
decisions.tradeoff: Your equipped weapon is only the current loadout, not your usual CoX switch. Check whether you already bring the lance and agree room roles. The lance lacks the hasta's special attack; it does not replace a separate defence-reduction plan.
decisions.effort: Small kit review using owned gear; practice and inventory choices vary. No Hydra grind is suggested.
decisions.access: Comparing equipment has no game requirement. Wielding a lance requires 78 Attack plus the Firemaking (not pyre), Fishing and Smithing sections of Barbarian Training; the levels are checked, the miniquest sections are unknown. Actual raid access and other kit preparation remain unverified.
decisions.completion: Currently equipped lance or observed scythe/Soulreaper axe suppresses this comparison. This is a temporary loadout state, not permanent account completion.
decisions.applicability: Owned lance and a recognised ordinary melee alternative, Attack 78+, known equipment without lance, and no recognised competing melee weapon in observed storage.
decisions.preparation: Owned lance and a recognised ordinary melee alternative, Attack 78+, known equipment without lance, and no recognised competing melee weapon in observed storage.
decisions.benefitReason: Owned dragonbane alternative for the Olm melee role.

decisions.title: Agree team defence-reduction coverage with your owned gear
decisions.why: You have recognised weapons across three styles and an owned defence-reduction weapon. Agreeing who brings which option is useful for established CoX teams as well as learners. Bowfa, a better staff or a lance does not establish the team's special-attack coverage.
decisions.alternative: A dragon warhammer, Bandos godsword and elder maul are current options with different drains and equipment costs. An owned elder maul avoids treating a warhammer as a mandatory new grind; BGS remains a complementary team option. If teammates cover the role, agree whether your inventory space is better used for supplies.
decisions.tradeoff: Defence reduction depends on the encounter and successful specials; these weapons are not interchangeable guarantees. Team loadouts and coverage are unknown. This is pre-raid planning, without live combat cues or certification of access, supplies or player skill.
decisions.effort: Small recurring team discussion using owned gear; no shaman, Bandos or raid-drop grind is required.
decisions.access: Planning has no game requirement. DWH wielding requires 60 Strength; BGS 75 Attack; elder maul 75 Attack and 75 Strength. The authored three-style planning baseline is preparation, not raid entry. Actual CoX access remains unverified.
decisions.completion: Repeatable team coordination; no team history or permanent completion is inferred.
decisions.applicability: The same recognised weapon and skill baseline as team planning, plus an observed reduction option and its wield levels. This more specific prompt shares the broad team-planning family.
notes: The checked skill and three-style baseline is authored preparation, not game access. Team roles, full raid switches, supplies and actual access remain unverified.
decisions.preparation: The same recognised weapon and skill baseline as team planning, plus an observed reduction option and its wield levels. This more specific prompt shares the broad team-planning family.
decisions.benefitReason: Specific observed team coverage before general team planning.

decisions.title: Review an owned occult switch for your CoX mage kit
decisions.why: You have an occult necklace and a recognised charged magic weapon, while a fury is currently equipped. The occult supplies magic damage that the fury does not. Checking this switch can help an established Bowfa or staff account without another gear grind.
decisions.alternative: Keep the fury as a simpler hybrid switch if inventory space or switch complexity matters more. If you already bring the occult for mage, this review is already handled; current equipment cannot reveal your saved raid kit. An ornamented occult has the same combat stats.
decisions.tradeoff: A more specialised switch costs inventory space and attention; do not replace your melee/ranged necklace for all styles. The equipment observation is a prompt to review, not proof that you have forgotten your occult.
decisions.effort: Small owned-kit review with no Slayer grind or exact damage forecast; the benefit depends on the full loadout.
decisions.access: Wearing the occult requires 70 Magic. A recognised magic weapon and its wield level are checked. Owning an occult does not impose a Slayer requirement; acquiring it from smoke devils is outside this owned-kit comparison.
decisions.completion: Occult currently equipped suppresses this prompt; no usual raid setup or permanent loadout completion is inferred.
decisions.applicability: Positive occult observation, currently equipped normal/ornamented fury, Magic 70+, recognised charged magic weapon with its level. Empty or unknown equipment produces no suggestion.
decisions.preparation: Positive occult observation, currently equipped normal/ornamented fury, Magic 70+, recognised charged magic weapon with its level. Empty or unknown equipment produces no suggestion.
decisions.benefitReason: Owned specialised magic alternative to the equipped hybrid necklace.

decisions.title: Consider CG for a Bowfa and crystal-armour route
decisions.why: You have confirmed the covered Bowfa/twisted-bow gap. CG offers an enhanced seed and armour seeds without consuming your outside combat supplies. This is an optional long ranged route for several supported activities.
decisions.alternative: If CG is unwelcome, Moons offers an eclipse atlatl route when its access and your melee preparation are supported. A rune crossbow also remains a planning option for low-level ToA and ordinary team CoX; an atlatl is not a universal Bowfa substitute.
decisions.tradeoff: Repeated solo encounters and learning compete with Slayer, Zulrah and raid practice. Crystal armour and shard upkeep matter; no player skill or RNG progress is inferred.
decisions.effort: Long variable drop grind plus learning and shards. Start with regular Gauntlet if learning; CG first requires one regular completion, which is not observed. No hours or completion probability.
decisions.access: Song of the Elves completion permits Gauntlet access. This is a route starting with the regular unlock, not proof CG is already enterable. Weapons and supplies are made inside. Bowfa creation needs the seed/shards; NPC singing is available for extra shards instead of mandatory Crafting/Smithing levels.
decisions.completion: A supported Bowfa form or twisted bow owned suppresses another enhanced-seed route. It does not establish complete crystal armour or usable charges.
decisions.preparation: Authored learning baseline: 80 Attack/Strength/Defence/Hitpoints, 85 Ranged/Magic, 70 Prayer. Higher prayers are helpful, not access requirements. Crystal body/legs/helm and 70 Agility need checking before using the reward.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: You have confirmed the covered Bowfa/twisted-bow gap. CG offers an enhanced seed and armour seeds without consuming your outside combat supplies. This is an optional long ranged route for several supported activities.

decisions.title: Train Slayer toward 87 for the first seas trident route
decisions.why: A confirmed powered-staff gap can make Slayer progression a shared investment for ToA and ordinary team CoX. Reaching 87 opens the cave-kraken task route; the level alone does not award a trident.
decisions.alternative: Continue with reviewed owned spell options and lower-level content, or use Royal Titans for a prayer upgrade. Zulrah upgrades a seas trident; it is not a source of the base seas trident.
decisions.tradeoff: A long skill and task route delays immediate boss practice. No efficient universal task list, supplies or task availability are inferred.
decisions.effort: Supply- and task-dependent training; no exact hours. This milestone is a prerequisite, not random-drop completion.
decisions.access: Ordinary Slayer training. Obtaining cave kraken tasks later requires 87 Slayer and 50 Magic; task assignment and current tasks are not read.
decisions.completion: Real Slayer at least 87 completes this training step, while actual trident acquisition remains a separate decision.
decisions.preparation: Authored scope: known Slayer level and 75 Magic to make the future seas-trident objective meaningful. Task-specific gear, access and supplies need separate review.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: A confirmed powered-staff gap can make Slayer progression a shared investment for ToA and ordinary team CoX. Reaching 87 opens the cave-kraken task route; the level alone does not award a trident.

decisions.title: Seek a cave-kraken task for your first seas trident
decisions.why: You meet the task-level thresholds and confirmed that no covered seas trident or competing magic option is owned. Small cave krakens offer a first-trident route useful to multiple raid goals.
decisions.alternative: The Kraken boss can also drop a charged trident on the same task, with a different reward mix; small cave krakens are a credible first-trident choice. An owned swamp/Sanguinesti/Ayak/Shadow/wand option avoids this bounded grind.
decisions.tradeoff: Task assignment and the weapon drop are both uncertain. A task is required to fight the monsters; this card asks you to seek one and does not claim an active task.
decisions.effort: Variable task/drop route. Charge the eventual weapon with its required runes and coins; no charges or quantities are inferred.
decisions.access: 87 Slayer and 50 Magic permit cave-kraken task assignment. Killing cave krakens also needs that task. The current task is unobserved. Seas trident use requires 75 Magic; do not infer it from components.
decisions.completion: A supported seas trident or competing magic option owned ends this acquisition route, including uncharged forms for ownership only.
decisions.preparation: Authored route scope: 75 Magic for eventual use. Arrange a usable magic spell setup and task supplies; the card does not claim a combat loadout.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: You meet the task-level thresholds and confirmed that no covered seas trident or competing magic option is owned. Small cave krakens offer a first-trident route useful to multiple raid goals.

decisions.title: Consider Zulrah for a magic-fang upgrade
decisions.why: Your observed seas trident can support a Zulrah route toward a swamp trident. A Bowfa account can still have this magic gap; the upgrade helps both supported raid goals.
decisions.alternative: Keep the seas trident if scale upkeep or Zulrah is unwelcome. Review an owned competing magic option first; Royal Titans offers a prayer route without requiring this fang.
decisions.tradeoff: Solo learning and scale/rune upkeep compete with raid practice and Slayer. A magic fang is not a guaranteed drop, and stronger magic equipment is not always necessary to start raids.
decisions.effort: Variable solo drop grind, learning and recurring supplies. Fang assembly is a separate small action once the parts are owned.
decisions.access: The game requires Regicide progress through reaching Port Tyras and the sacrifice dialogue. This slice conservatively confirms completed Regicide; partial progress/dialogue remain unobserved. Assembly later requires 59 Crafting and a chisel; these are not Zulrah entry requirements.
decisions.completion: A swamp trident or supported competing magic option owned suppresses this weapon route. An already observed magic fang also suppresses further fang acquisition.
decisions.preparation: Authored hybrid baseline: 75 Magic, 80 Ranged, 70 Defence, 80 Hitpoints and 45 Prayer; observed usable seas trident plus ranged alternative. Supplies, venom handling, spellbook and switches still need review.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: Your observed seas trident can support a Zulrah route toward a swamp trident. A Bowfa account can still have this magic gap; the upgrade helps both supported raid goals.

decisions.title: Start low-level ToA practice toward a fang
decisions.why: Your supported observed three-style options and access allow planning low-level ToA practice while working toward its fang reward. Bowfa is optional and the raid reward is not an entry prerequisite.
decisions.alternative: Use the owned base keris partisan for its specialist role and a reviewed melee alternative elsewhere. Stay at a comfortable raid level or choose Zulrah/Slayer/Royal Titans for shared upgrades first; none guarantees raid success.
decisions.tradeoff: Practice, supplies and random rewards compete with targeted gear routes. Entry-level learning is useful without promising an efficient fang grind or solo/Expert readiness.
decisions.effort: Repeat practice followed by a variable reward route. Learning/team size/raid level change effort; no drop or hour estimate. Team or solo low-level assumptions must be agreed by the player.
decisions.access: Beneath Cursed Sands completion is the raid access requirement. Fang ownership, Bowfa, Rigour, Augury and defence-reduction weapons are not entry requirements.
decisions.completion: An owned normal or ornamented Osmumten's fang ends this bounded acquisition goal; ownership does not certify levels, supply readiness or a completed raid.
decisions.preparation: Authored low-level planning baseline: 70 Attack/Strength/Defence/Prayer, 80 Ranged and 75 Magic; observed base keris partisan, melee, ranged and powered-magic alternatives. Other keris forms and full loadouts are outside this slice.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: Your supported observed three-style options and access allow planning low-level ToA practice while working toward its fang reward. Bowfa is optional and the raid reward is not an entry prerequisite.

contextBenefits.reason: An observed ranged alternative already supports some planning; the atlatl is a contextual additional option.

decisions.title: Consider Moons for an eclipse atlatl alternative
decisions.why: With a confirmed ranged gap and supported melee preparation, Moons offers an eclipse atlatl acquisition route without CG. Its ranged accuracy and strength-based damage make it a contextual option, not a universal weapon ladder.
decisions.alternative: Keep the rune crossbow for shield/bolt setups or choose CG for Bowfa and crystal. Existing Bowfa/twisted-bow ownership suppresses this narrow alternative grind. Atlatl ammunition and strength gear need review for each encounter.
decisions.tradeoff: The atlatl is a random chest reward. Moons favours defensive melee gear and uses local food/potions, but complete armour and supplies are not inferred. The atlatl does not replace Bowfa at every boss.
decisions.effort: Variable chest grind and learning. Local supply gathering can reduce outside consumable costs; no exact time or RNG percentage.
decisions.access: Complete Perilous Moons to claim the Lunar Chest. Atlatl use needs 75 Ranged, 50 Attack and 50 Strength; these are reward wield requirements, not chest access requirements.
decisions.completion: An owned atlatl or supported Bowfa/twisted-bow alternative ends this optional ranged route. Charges, armour, ammo and usability remain separate.
decisions.preparation: Authored baseline: 70 Attack/Strength/Defence, 75 Hitpoints/Ranged, 50 Herblore and a supported observed melee weapon. Herblore helps local potion supplies; it is optional preparation, not dungeon access.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: With a confirmed ranged gap and supported melee preparation, Moons offers an eclipse atlatl acquisition route without CG. Its ranged accuracy and strength-based damage make it a contextual option, not a universal weapon ladder.

notes: Read a positively observed relevant intermediate-prayer scroll before starting another acquisition route. Unknown other storage still needs checking.
decisions.title: Consider Royal Titans for intermediate prayer unlocks
decisions.why: A confirmed intermediate-prayer gap can help both magic and ranged preparation without a CoX scroll drop. Bowfa ownership does not remove the usefulness of better available prayers.
decisions.alternative: Use currently unlocked prayers or work toward Rigour/Augury through CoX. If the stronger prayer is already unlocked for a style, target the other useful style instead. Do not treat intermediate prayers as mandatory raid entry.
decisions.tradeoff: Duo contribution and random rewards affect effort. Loot Eldric for Deadeye and Branda for Mystic Vigour; an owned scroll should be read instead of farming another. Higher prayers can make the intermediate route unnecessary.
decisions.effort: Variable duo drop route plus a one-off read. No exact hours; this card assumes a partner, not inferred solo ability.
decisions.access: Royal Titans have no quest/skill entry requirement. Using Deadeye needs 62 Prayer and Mystic Vigour 63; the authored kit baseline is optional preparation. 60 Agility is a shortcut, not entry.
decisions.completion: For each style, the intermediate prayer or its higher Rigour/Augury unlock satisfies this bounded target. Permanent unlock facts, not consumed-scroll absence, determine completion.
decisions.preparation: Authored duo baseline: 70 Attack/Strength/Defence/Ranged/Hitpoints, 75 Magic and 63 Prayer, supported observed melee/ranged options. Arrange standard elemental spells, runes and supplies; a powered staff alone does not establish the required spell setup.
decisions.applicability: Only a confirmed target gap and positively supported conditions make this actionable; unknown ownership abstains.
decisions.benefitReason: A confirmed intermediate-prayer gap can help both magic and ranged preparation without a CoX scroll drop. Bowfa ownership does not remove the usefulness of better available prayers.
